dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi, Kevin, yes, hi. This is Celeste Fortes. I'm calling about the water, you know, the pooling water at the corner by my place. It's 261 Kay Street, up Historic Hill. Right, do you know the area?
Kay Street, sure. Okay, 261 Kay. What's going on there, Celeste?

So, I mean, ever since that snow-to-rain storm, the one Sunday into Monday, the drain at the corner isn't taking anything. There's a big puddle, and I mean big, right across the crosswalk where the school bus stop is. And the kids, you know, they can't get across without stepping in it, so they're stepping out into the road to go around. Right? Cars come through there.
Yeah, that's not great. Okay, so water across the crosswalk by the bus stop, kids walking out into the street to get around it. I'm writing that down. Is it still standing now, today?

Still there. I looked ten minutes ago. It's Tuesday, the storm was done yesterday, and it's just sitting. And this isn't the first time, I mean, this corner does this every time we get a decent rain. I own the shop down the block and I watch it. Nobody ever comes, you know?
Understood. Is it the drain itself that's blocked, do you think? Leaves, slush, ice?

Well, I can't tell, there's so much water on it. But there's also, um, a manhole cover right there, kind of in the street edge, and it looks off to me. Like it's sitting maybe an inch higher or lower than the pavement around it. Right? You follow me? Like it's not seated right.
Okay, manhole cover looks off by about an inch. That's worth noting separately, because a cover that's not flush can be a hazard. Is it in the travel lane or by the curb?
Closer to the curb, but the kids are walking right around it. A car hits that, I mean, I don't know what happens.
Got it. Let me put all that in. Cross street, do you know it, or is it right at your number?
It's right at the corner by 261, the bus stop side. That's the crosswalk I mean. I can see it from the sidewalk.
Perfect. I've got the crosswalk at 261 Kay Street, standing water, drain not taking it, plus the manhole cover not sitting flush.
Right, right. So will you open a work order? And what date, I mean, can you tell me a date somebody's coming? Because I've heard, you know, we'll send somebody, and then nothing.

Yes, I'm opening a work order now, one for the drain and one flagged for the manhole cover. As for the date, the crews are working through a pile of calls from the storm. I'd say realistically in the next few days for a first look, and the drain would probably be first since it's near a bus stop.

A few days. Okay. I mean, the kids are out there every morning. My niece has a science fair thing this week, a volcano with baking soda, and she was telling me she nearly walked into the road with the poster board, you know, avoiding that water. That's what I mean.
Yeah, that's exactly the kind of detail that helps. I'll note the school bus stop and the kids stepping into the road so it gets looked at sooner. Do you want a callback when it's scheduled?
Yes, please. It's 401-555-0176.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one seven six. And that's Celeste Fortes, right?
Right, Fortes, F-O-R-T-E-S. And you'll call with the date?
I'll note it on the order so whoever schedules it calls you with the date. If you see it get worse, or somebody actually gets hurt, call back right away and we'll push it.
Okay. Okay, thank you, Kevin. I just, you know, I'd like it fixed this time.
Understood. Order's in. You take care, Celeste.
